title: FSR: SOA Voltage Limit Monitoring with Debounce

safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: foxBMS 2 publishes no functional safety requirements with identifiers. This record was written by this corpus from the safe-operating-area comparison code in the pinned source; the project stated no such obligation and allocated nothing.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees a safety requirement at ASIL_D with a mapping to ISO 26262 Part 4 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the product's voltage-limit monitoring is a reviewed, allocated, ASIL_D requirement. It is a back-inference from the comparison code, and the record's own fault_reaction.open_limits records that the configured debounce counts and delays make the reaction longer than the 100 ms the goal above it allocates - a contradiction the corpus recorded rather than resolved.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81-146 (SOA_CheckVoltages) for the three-tier limit comparison and the tiered DIAG_Handler escalation; src/app/application/soa/soa.c:271-351 (SOA_CheckCurrent) and src/app/application/soa/soa.c:148-269 (SOA_CheckTemperatures) for the current and temperature halves; src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:341-475 (DIAG_Handler) for the debounce the reaction actually waits on. All at the pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source compares cell values against configured limits and reports a violation, and that the debounce sits in DIAG_Handler. It does NOT support the ASIL_D allocation or the 10 ms comparison budget, and it is the evidence that CONTRADICTS the goal's 100 ms FTTI rather than supporting it.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction this requirement was missing, derived from the source. The reaction is the real one and it is graded: SOA_CheckVoltages() at src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81-131 compares against a three-tier MOL/RSL/MSL limit set and raises the corresponding DIAG entry, and only the MSL tier is configured DIAG_FATAL_ERROR (src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:126-131) - the RSL tier is DIAG_WARNING and the MOL tier DIAG_INFO, both with DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD. An excursion into the RSL or MOL band therefore produces a recorded diagnosis and no contactor opening. That graded behaviour is a real part of the reaction and is recorded rather than flattened into a single claim. The time figures are given with their basis and are explicitly not the synthetic figures: the debounce in front of the reaction is the DIAG occurrence counter rather than a count maintained by the SOA module, and the delay is DIAG_DELAY_200ms. open_limits records one contradiction that this field does NOT resolve and that a reader must not be left unaware of: this record's statement specifies a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms and a 5 ms classification, and FB2-PRM-000006 records soa_debounce_count = 2, but the source implements no counter in the SOA module and configures the MSL tier at 50 events with a 200 ms delay, and no 5 ms classification figure exists in bms_cfg.h or diag_cfg.c. The statement, the acceptance criteria and the parameter registry were deliberately NOT edited: a requirement that does not match its implementation is a different finding from a missing fault reaction, and deciding which of the two is authoritative is a decision this pass has no evidence base for. It is recorded here so the fault_reaction cannot be read as confirming the statement's figures. Statement, rationale, all four acceptance criteria, safety_allocation, the ASIL and the safety goal reference are unchanged and no threshold was relaxed. Human approval remains pending, production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false.

statement: The BMS shall monitor each cell voltage against configured minimum and maximum limits with a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms, and classify violations within 5 ms of data availability, triggering FAULT state request on confirmed violation.
rationale: SOA monitoring must detect limit violations fast enough to meet FTTI

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from database read to violation classification

fault_reaction.reaction: Set the corresponding diagnosis entry, and if that entry's configured severity is DIAG_FATAL_ERROR, drive the battery state machine into the latched error state, which opens the HV contactors. The path is: SOA_CheckVoltages() in src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81 compares the per-string minimum and maximum cell voltages against the three-tier limits and calls DIAG_Handler for the tier that was crossed; the DIAG module latches the entry once its occurrence counter passes the configured sensitivity; BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet() at src/app/application/bms/bms.c:515-531 walks the fatal-error table built at src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:254-260; BMS_IsBatterySystemStateOkay() at bms.c:534-575 returns STD_NOT_OK after the shortest active delay has elapsed; and the state machine is set to BMS_FSM_STATE_OPEN_CONTACTORS with nextState BMS_FSM_STATE_ERROR at bms.c:1197-1204. Only the MSL tier reaches that path: DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_OVERVOLTAGE_MSL and DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_UNDERVOLTAGE_MSL are configured DIAG_FATAL_ERROR, while the RSL tier is DIAG_WARNING and the MOL tier is DIAG_INFO, and both non-MSL tiers carry DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD (src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:126-131). An excursion into the RSL or MOL band therefore produces a recorded diagnosis and no contactor opening, which is a real graded reaction and not an omission.
fault_reaction.triggered_by: A cell voltage crossing BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MOL_mV, BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_RSL_mV or BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MSL_mV, or the corresponding minimum limits, evaluated in SOA_CheckVoltages() at src/app/application/soa/soa.c:89-131. Whether the crossing produces a reaction at all, and which one, is decided by the configured severity of the corresponding entry, not by the comparison.
fault_reaction.reaction_time_budget_basis: DIAG_DELAY_200ms from diag_cfg.c:126 and diag_cfg.c:129. This is the delay between the entry becoming active and the state request, and it is the delay for a DIAG_FATAL_ERROR entry, not the whole reaction. The debounce in front of it is a count, not a time: DIAG_SEN_EVENT_50 is a threshold of 49 and DIAG_GetDiagnosisEntryState at src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:287-301 activates the entry when occurrenceCounter > 49. The evaluations are driven once per BMS_Trigger from src/app/application/bms/bms.c:913, and the BMS task period is BMS_STATEMACHINE_TASK_CYCLE_CONTEXT_MS = 10 ms (src/app/application/config/bms_cfg.h:100), so 50 evaluations is of the order of 500 ms and the state request follows roughly 700 ms after a sustained excursion. That figure is read off the configuration, not measured.
fault_reaction.mode_dependence: Mode-independent as to the mechanism: SOA_CheckVoltages() is called on every BMS_Trigger regardless of mode (bms.c:911-917). The consequence is mode-dependent: opening the contactors in MOD-004, where current is flowing to a moving vehicle, removes propulsion, which is the caveat FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 records against the AR-004 reaction.
fault_reaction.allocation_basis: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.fault_reaction entry 3 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.fault_reaction allocate the latched FAULT mode to AR-002 at 3 ms. The 3 ms is the synthetic_reference allocation and does NOT describe the real implementation, which has no equivalent 3 ms step: the real path from a sustained excursion to a state request is a counter threshold plus a configured delay, configured at src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:126 and read at bms.c:534-575. Both figures are recorded here rather than one being dropped, because the synthetic figure is what the synthetic concepts allocate and the configured figure is what the source does.
fault_reaction.open_limits: One contradiction is recorded and it is NOT resolved by this field, because resolving it is a different piece of work with its own evidence requirement. This record's statement specifies 'a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms' and 'classify violations within 5 ms of data availability', and FB2-PRM-000006 records soa_debounce_count = 2, which is where those figures come from. The source does not implement them. src/app/application/soa/soa.c implements a three-tier MOL/RSL/MSL comparison with no counter in the SOA module at all, and the debounce that does exist is the DIAG occurrence counter, configured at 50 events for the MSL tier (diag_cfg.c:126). There is no 5 ms classification figure in either bms_cfg.h or diag_cfg.c. The statement, the acceptance criteria and the parameter registry have NOT been edited, because the statement is a requirement and a requirement that does not match the implementation is a different finding from a missing fault reaction, and closing it requires a decision about which of the two is authoritative. It is recorded here so that a reader of this reaction is not left believing that the 100 ms debound and 5 ms classification are implemented behaviour. Also unresolved: no measurement of the counter threshold, the delay or the state transition exists in this corpus.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Diagnostic callbacks, independent HW monitor, plausibility

provenance_note: Provenance re-checked 2026-10-01 after the source-registry repair. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000004, -000005 and -000006 previously named SOA_CheckVoltageLimits, SOA_CheckCurrentLimits and SOA_CheckTemperatureLimits, none of which exists; they now name SOA_CheckVoltages (soa.c:81-146), SOA_CheckCurrent (soa.c:271-351) and SOA_CheckTemperatures (soa.c:148-269), which do perform the configured-limit comparison and the DIAG escalation this requirement is about. Origin remains source_observed. The debounce (2 violations within 100 ms) and the 5 ms classification latency are modelled back-inferred values, not established by any anchor.

asil_allocation_scope.classification_belongs_to: the hypothetical reference project declared by the synthetic_reference profile of this corpus
asil_allocation_scope.statement: The asil value in this record's safety_allocation is a RECONSTRUCTED value, not an observation and not a determination. It was produced by reading back the safety-goal classification of the hypothetical reference project this corpus also declares in its synthetic_reference profile, and by attributing that classification to this record because this corpus's own requirement set was written downstream of it. The real foxBMS 2 product has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment. No HARA has been performed for it, none is claimed here, and nothing in this record may be read as one, as a partial one, or as a substitute for one.
asil_allocation_scope.why_the_value_is_still_here: The ASIL is retained rather than deleted because it is legitimate inside the fictional project: the reference project needs an allocated class at this element for its own argument to be internally consistent, and removing the number would leave the reference project's allocation silently unallocated. What was illegitimate was its presentation here, as an unqualified field on an as_is record that a reader could take as a statement about the product. That presentation is what this field removes.
what_this_field_asserts: That the recorded asil value equals the classification the reference project's safety concept and goal chain assigns to this element, as those records state it.
That the classification originates in the reference project and nowhere else.
That no classification has been performed for the real product by this corpus or by anyone on its behalf.
what_this_field_does_not_assert: It does not assert an ASIL for the real foxBMS 2 product. The real product's safety integrity level is undetermined, not ASIL_D; undetermined is the honest answer and this corpus has no standing to change it.
It does not assert that a hazard analysis and risk assessment exists for the real product in any form, complete or partial.

It does not assert that any design, in either profile, meets this ASIL. An allocation creates an obligation downstream; it is not evidence the obligation is discharged, and no execution record in this corpus discharges it for this element.
It does not assert ISO 26262 conformity, certification, or qualification of any product, supplier, tool or process.
It does not assert an Automotive SPICE capability level for any organisation.

It does not assert that the exposure or severity inputs behind the reference project's classification are evidenced. They are authored: the reference project's safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 already records that its exposure rating is an unevidenced authored input and that a single exposure step would move the whole classification one class lower.
asil_allocation_scope.reading_rule: Any view, report or export that renders this record's asil value must render this field with it. An asil value shown without this field is a defect in that view, not a permissible abbreviation.
asil_allocation_scope.origin_field_relationship: Because this record now carries a back-inferred classification alongside its source-derived content, origin is 'derived' rather than 'source_observed': master prompt section 5 requires that an artefact containing both observed and modelled content must not be labelled wholly observed. Where this record's origin was 'source_observed' it has been changed to 'derived' for that reason and for no other; no statement, acceptance criterion, threshold, assumption, safety goal reference or mitigation text was altered in the same edit.
